title: Calibrating Treatment Effect Estimators in First-In-First-Out Enrollment at Critical Capacity
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: incremental < field; mathematics and four cited sources pass, but paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4 and no bounded same-scope repair.
gap_reasons: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR (triage, round 0) — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope, so the directed-revise loop was stopped before spending its budget on a note that cannot clear the bar.

The substantive contribution is the derived exact-weight FIFO boundary law and feasible calibration for one constant-probability, single-batch design under cumulative endpoint regularity; broader queue inference is not established.

Operational significance remains un demonstrated: the specified cutoff requires n at least 65,536 even at K=0, so both intervals use the full-causal-range fallback throughout the reported simulation sizes and at the housing anchor's cohort size.
Panel findings left unrepaired (the tier, not these, is the reason for the halt): ballast@thm:certified-calibration-realization.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and reviewed the raw fixed-roster FIFO boundary law, observable calibration, feasible count correction, and restricted count-projection optimality; the math panel passed and all four cited claims were verified after primary-source attestations. The field-floor claim failed at the authoritative incremental assessment (paper-score ceiling 6.2 < 7.4), with narrow single-batch scope and an informative calibration cutoff beyond the cited applied cohort; ballast remains disclosed. No F-stage or Lean proof was attempted; retain as sound informal lower-tier science for a separately authorized re-anchor, not an accepted theorem.
tldr: For a fixed FIFO enrollment batch at critical capacity, a feasible original-record correction removes the complete nonlinear flag-count response and is asymptotically optimal among regular corrections with square-integrable count-measurable limits. Its limiting mean squared error is uniquely minimized by that response; centered limiting variance has the same unique minimizer. The enabling results derive the raw exact-marginal Horvitz--Thompson law, including non-Gaussian witnesses and second moments, and provide a total original-record nonlinear 95 percent confidence calibration. The corrected estimator has an independent Gaussian residual law and its own covariance-robust calibration. Every guarantee concerns the same fixed potential-outcome roster and public flag design.
gap: Published priority-queue inference uses an iid cohort and outcome-residual conditioning. It does not give the conditional fixed-table law of raw exact-marginal HT at critical capacity. Marginal rearrangement variance bounds do not evaluate its nonlinear tails or supply feasible removal of its count response.
fill: The package derives the raw actual law and mandatory nonlinear confidence interval, then uses that expansion to construct a feasible count correction with Gaussian residual inference and an exact asymptotic variance comparison on the same design. Endpoint and bulk-score nuisance rates, numerical centering and both calibration algorithms are proved from the original record. No empirical-law convergence rate or observed joint potential-outcome covariance is imposed.
